title: The CLI rebuilds its whole argparse tree on every invocation
findings_note: profiled; I first misattributed this to store.load

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
`cli.main` calls `build_parser()` every time, which constructs ~28 subparsers from
scratch. A cProfile of the full test suite puts **31 of 43 seconds inside
`build_parser`**, and 16 of those inside `gettext` — argparse does a locale lookup for
every argument's help string as it builds each subparser. One build measures ~17ms.

    780  ...  cli.py:545(build_parser)      cumtime 31.1s
  23403  ...  argparse __init__            cumtime 26.0s
  69435  ...  gettext.dgettext             cumtime 16.0s

The suite runs `main()` 780 times in one process, so it pays that 780 times — which is
why 327 tests take ~45s while any single module runs in under a tenth of a second. For a
one-shot CLI the cost is ~17ms of cold start, minor but free to remove; for an agent or
a future watch/REPL mode calling `main()` in-process it is the whole story.

I flagged this earlier as `store.load` reading every slice on every run. That was wrong:
`store.load` measures 0.15ms. The cost is entirely parser construction.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. `build_parser` returns a usable parser and `main` still dispatches every command.
2. A perf guard: `main` invoked N times builds the parser at most once (assert
   `build_parser` is called once across repeated `main` calls, via a counter or a patch).

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Build the parser once and reuse it. A single parser instance handles repeated
`parse_args` safely — confirmed: `parse_args` populates a fresh namespace and does not
mutate the parser. Memoize at module scope (or a cached module-level singleton that
`main` reuses). Keep `build_parser` callable for tests that want a fresh one.

Watch the two subtleties: the `--root` argument uses `default=argparse.SUPPRESS` on the
subparser copy so it does not clobber the global one — that behaviour must survive
reuse — and `set_defaults(func=...)` is set at build time, so a cached parser keeps the
right dispatch. A test asserting both is worth having.

**Not in this slice:** replacing argparse, or lazy help text. Caching is the whole win
and stays stdlib.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
The suite drops sharply (build once, not 780 times) and every command still parses and
dispatches. Cold-start `slicer --help` is unchanged in behaviour.
